topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture with an introduction from the lecturer and an outline of the learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, examining the balance between endogenous bad luck and environmental exposures across global populations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing on direct mechanisms and the specific etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical agents cause DNA damage directly or through endogenous metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, microenvironmental factors, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms that advance carcinogenesis, including tumor promotion pathways, inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey experimental, genomic, and epidemiological approaches for detecting carcinogenic agents and assessing their real-world risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the lecture.
